items.title: Stiff Extracellular Matrix Rejuvenates Aged Mesenchymal Stem Cells via PI3K-AKT Signaling.
items.abstract: Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) are widely used to modulate immune responses and promote tissue regeneration, but cellular senescence significantly impairs their therapeutic potential. MSCs undergo senescence characterized by an enlarged morphology, reduced proliferative capacity, and altered expression of genes related to the cytoskeleton. This study revealed that the mechanical microenvironment critically regulates MSC aging. Culturing senescent MSCs on high-stiffness extracellular matrix (ECM) hydrogels reverses key aspects of the senescent phenotype, including the restoration of normal morphology, improved cytoskeletal integrity, and enhanced proliferation. This mechanical rescue is accompanied by genetic reprogramming and activation of the PI3K-AKT signaling pathway. The inhibition of PI3K-Akt with LY294002 abolished these rejuvenating effects. These findings demonstrate that the mechanical microenvironment can reprogram senescent MSCs through PI3K-AKT-mediated mechanotransduction, offering a novel strategy to restore stem cell function in aging and regenerative medicine.

items.title: Microvascular Resistance Reserve and Outcomes in Angina and Nonobstructive Coronary Artery Disease.
items.abstract: Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is highly prevalent in patients with angina and nonobstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA). Microvascular resistance reserve (MRR) is a novel index to assess CMD independently of epicardial disease and driving pressures, but the long-term prognostic value of continuous thermodilution-derived MRR in patients with ANOCA is unknown. To assess the prognostic value of continuous thermodilution-derived MRR and its association with clinical outcomes and symptom burden in patients with ANOCA. This prospective, multicenter cohort study within the Netherlands Registry of Invasive Coronary Vasomotor Function Testing (NL-CFT) included patients between July 2020 and June 2025 in 4 clinical centers in the Netherlands. Follow-up for clinical events and patient-reported symptoms was completed for up to 3 years. Clinical events were adjudicated by investigators blinded to CFT results. Consecutive patients with ANOCA who underwent continuous thermodilution were included. Abnormal MRR (CMD) was defined as less than 2.1, gray zone as 2.1 to 2.7, and normal microvascular function as 2.7 or greater. The primary clinical outcome was a composite of all-cause death, acute coronary syndrome, stroke, clinically indicated revascularization, repeat angiography without intervention, and unplanned hospital admittance or emergency department visit due to angina or heart failure. Secondary outcomes included angina at baseline and follow-up. Symptoms were assessed using the patient-reported Seattle Angina Questionnaire (SAQ) scores. Among 553 included patients (mean [SD] age, 59.1 [9.6] years; 459 female [83.0%]) with a mean (SD) follow-up of 27.5 (16.1) months, CMD was observed in 94 patients (17.0%). The main composite outcome did not differ across the 3 MRR categories (18 of 94 patients with abnormal [19.1%] vs 21 of 98 patients with gray zone [21.4%] vs 76 of 361 patients with normal [21.1%] MRR; log-rank P = .85). Individual outcomes did not differ between groups. There was no overall longitudinal interaction between MRR and SAQ summary scores. While low MRR (abnormal vs normal groups) was not associated with an increased symptom burden at baseline, it was associated with worse angina at follow-up (mean [SD] SAQ summary score, 53.0 [16.7] vs 60.1 [16.6]; P = .04) and less clinically relevant improvement (9 of 30 patients [30.0%] vs 52 of 88 patients [59.1%]; P = .02). In this study, CMD assessed by continuous thermodilution-derived MRR was not associated with clinical outcomes.

items.title: Behavior-Based Electrogram Mapping Identifies Potential Functional Substrates in Atrial Fibrillation: The KSP-AF Randomized Study.
items.abstract: Conventional substrate mapping during atrial fibrillation (AF) may fail to capture dynamic electrogram behavior. Key spatiotemporal potentials (KSPs) are electrogram patterns identified by their temporal behavior during AF. We evaluated whether KSP-guided ablation improves outcomes beyond pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) and characterized their short-term frequency consistency. In this single-center randomized study, 100 patients with paroxysmal or persistent AF undergoing first-time ablation were assigned to PVI plus KSP-guided ablation or PVI alone. The primary endpoint was 24-month single-procedure freedom from documented AF recurrence without antiarrhythmic drugs. Dominant frequency (DF) analysis included 93 KSP regions from 18 patients, assessed across four consecutive 5-second epochs. Acute AF termination occurred in 68% of patients with PVI + KSP versus 26% with PVI alone (P < 0.001). At 24 months, freedom from AF recurrence was 74% versus 48% (HR 0.38, 95% CI 0.18-0.79; P = 0.010), and freedom from AF/atrial tachycardia recurrence was 68% versus 46% (HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.25-0.97; P = 0.040). Within-recording temporal DF variability was low (coefficient of variation, 4.8 ± 1.2%). Adding KSP-guided ablation to PVI improved acute and 24-month rhythm outcomes in this single-center trial. These findings support further evaluation of behavior-based mapping to identify potential functional AF substrates and require multicenter confirmation.

items.title: Bioinformatics Analysis to Reveal Potential Targets of Huntington's Disease.
items.abstract: Huntington's disease (HD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease resulted from the expansion of CAG repeats in huntingtin (HTT) gene and characterised by motor impairment, psychiatric disorders and cognitive decline. Currently, there are no available disease-modifying treatments. In this study, we performed an integrative analysis of HD datasets downloaded from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database using machine learning approaches, Mendelian randomisation (MR) and single cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis to elucidate underlying disease mechanisms. The machine learning algorithms of LASSO, random forest and SVM-RFE identified the decreased ADRA2A in HD. In addition, MR analysis revealed HD-associated proteins such as LILRA4 and UBE2D1, associated with immune response and ubiquitination metabolism, respectively. scRNA-seq analysis further identified the transcription factors of SOX4 and ETV1 through SCENIC analysis. Pseudotime trajectory analysis highlighted heparan sulphate sulfotransferase activity, involving genes CHST11, HS3ST3A1 and HS6ST3 that drive cell differentiation. Moreover, cell-cell communication analysis demonstrated enhanced NRG1/3-ERBB4 signalling pathway in HD. This study presents multiple potential targets for HD treatment but further experimental validation is required to confirm their functional relevance.

items.title: Prognostic value of right ventricular ejection fraction measured by cardiac magnetic resonance in patients with transthyretin amyloidosis.
items.abstract: Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) plays an important role in both the diagnosis and follow-up of patients with transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CM), as it provides information on cardiac function, structure, and tissue characterization. Moreover, it is the gold standard for right ventricular (RV) assessment. However, evidence regarding the prognostic value of RV systolic dysfunction in this population remains limited. To evaluate the prognostic value of right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) measured by CMR in patients with ATTR-CM. MéTODOS: This was a single-center, observational, retrospective cohort study. We included patients from an institutional ATTR-CM registry who underwent CMR within 6 months of diagnosis between 2011 and 2025. Patients with other types of amyloidosis were excluded. Clinical, biochemical, echocardiographic, and CMR variables were collected. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Kaplan-Meier curves were constructed according to the presence or absence of RV dysfunction on CMR, defined as RVEF <50%. Univariate and multivariable Cox regression models were performed to identify predictors of the primary endpoint. TAPSE was not included in the multivariable models to avoid collinearity. A total of 100 patients were included, with a median age of 79 years [IQR 73-84]; 84% were men. Median left ventricular ejection fraction was 50% [IQR 42-62], and median RVEF was 48% [IQR 38-57]. Patients with lower RVEF had higher all-cause mortality (log-rank p = 0.008, Figure). In the multivariable model including age, atrial fibrillation, and NT-proBNP, RVEF was independently associated with all-cause mortality (HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.92-0.98; p = 0.002, Table). In our cohort of patients with ATTR-CM, RVEF assessed by CMR was independently associated with all-cause mortality. These findings suggest that RV assessment may provide additional value for risk stratification in this population.

items.title: Macrophage-directed immunotherapy in Inflammatory bowel disease: advances in reprogramming intestinal phagocytes.
items.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic, relapsing inflammatory disorder characterized by dysregulation of the intestinal immune system, in which functional abnormalities of phagocytes such as macrophages play a critical role in pathogenesis. Although conventional therapies such as anti-tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) antibodies are widely used in clinical practice, they have limitations including low response rates and significant side effects, creating an urgent need for novel therapeutic strategies. In recent years, macrophage-directed immunotherapy has emerged as a cutting-edge approach for IBD treatment by reprogramming intestinal phagocytes to restore immune homeostasis. Unlike previous reviews that primarily focus on the M1/M2 polarization framework, this review integrates recent single-cell discoveries of novel macrophage subsets (e.g. SPP1 + and TREM2 + macrophages), systematically examines the crosstalk among signaling, epigenetic, and metabolic regulatory layers, and critically evaluates translational barriers from preclinical models to clinical application. By evaluating preclinical and clinical studies, we assess the potential and challenges of these strategies. Through in-depth analysis, this review aims to provide a theoretical basis for the development of more precise and effective immunotherapies for IBD and to point out future research directions. (Literature search: PubMed, Web of Science, and Embase; January 2000-December 2025.). Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), including Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis, is a long-term condition caused by the immune system attacking the gut. Current treatments do not work for everyone and can cause serious side effects. Macrophages are a type of immune cell that normally help heal the gut but become harmful in IBD. This review explains how scientists are trying to reprogram these cells to reduce inflammation and promote healing. We discuss several approaches, including using medicines, nanoparticles, gene editing, and cell therapy. We also highlight the challenges that must be solved before these treatments can reach patients, such as safety, cost, and manufacturing. Understanding these barriers will help guide future research and bring better treatments to people with IBD.

items.title: An extraction-free one-pot immunomagnetic-RPA-CRISPR/Cas13a platform for ultrasensitive detection of exosomal PD-L1.
items.abstract: Programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expressed on the surface of exosomes (exo) is a promising liquid biopsy biomarker for monitoring response to immunotherapy in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, existing detection methods are limited by insufficient sensitivity and complicated operation. To address this, we developed an extraction-free immunomagnetic recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA)-based one-pot high-sensitivity CRISPR/Cas13a platform (iMRO-HCRISPR) employing DNA-conjugated antibodies. Exosomes in blood were enriched with anti-CD63/CD81/CD9 antibody-conjugated magnetic beads and recognized by PD-L1-specific DNA-antibody probes; the probe DNA then underwent RPA amplification, in vitro transcription (IVT), and Cas13a trans-cleavage, achieving multi-level signal amplification with fluorescent readout. Toehold-mediated DNA affinity pull-down effectively reduced the detection background. The platform achieved a limit of detection (LOD) as low as 10 1 particles/mL (positive detection at the single-particle level), a limit of quantification (LOQ) of 10 3 particles/mL, and a quantitative range of 10 3 -10 11 particles/mL, with the entire process completed in a single closed tube without exosome isolation. Clinical validation demonstrated that the platform effectively distinguished HCC patients from healthy controls (P < 0.0001), with an area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC) of 0.964. This study provides robust technical support for the ultrasensitive detection of exosomal PD-L1 in HCC and for dynamic monitoring of immunotherapy response.

items.title: Baseline Spleen Volume is Independently Associated With Survival After CD19-Directed Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-Cell Therapy in Relapsed/Refractory Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma.
items.abstract: Clinical outcomes after CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy in patients with relapsed or refractory (r/r) diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) remain heterogeneous, underscoring the need for improved risk stratification. As CAR T-cell efficacy is shaped not only by tumor-intrinsic features, host-related factors may also contribute to outcome variability. The spleen, the largest secondary lymphoid organ and a key regulator of immune cell trafficking, is a biologically plausible yet underexplored imaging marker in this setting. We retrospectively analyzed 88 patients with r/r DLBCL and available baseline imaging who received commercial CD19-directed CAR T-cell products between September 2019 and July 2025. Spleen volume was analyzed as a continuous variable (per 100 mL), without dichotomization or prespecified cutoffs, and clinical outcomes were examined in relation to baseline spleen volume. With a median follow-up of 24.4 months, 2-year progression-free survival and overall survival were 40.9% and 56.4%, respectively. Higher baseline spleen volume was associated with inferior overall survival, a higher cumulative incidence of relapse/progression, and inferior post-progression survival. The 24-month risk of death increased progressively with increasing spleen volume. Baseline spleen volume remained independently associated with inferior overall survival after adjustment for established pretreatment risk factors (aHR 1.136 per 100 mL, 95% CI, 1.012-1.275; p = 0.030). Findings were consistent in sensitivity analyses including adjustment for BMI and after exclusion of patients with splenic lymphoma manifestations. Baseline spleen volume thus emerges as a readily available imaging-derived marker that could complement established risk factors and refine baseline risk stratification prior to CAR T-cell therapy in r/r DLBCL. Beyond the pretreatment setting, it also has potential utility for prognostication after relapse/progression.

items.title: The microbiome and brain metastasis in non-small cell lung cancer: A graded appraisal and a framework for prevention-oriented research.
items.abstract: Brain metastasis remains a major cause of mortality and treatment failure in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, current models of cerebral dissemination rarely integrate microbiome-dependent systemic and intratumoral biology.This Review examines the potential microbiome-brain metastasis axis linking gut, lung, and intratumoral microbial communities to intracranial dissemination and therapeutic response. A reproducible literature search was conducted to evaluate proposed mechanisms underlying microbiome-associated brain metastasis. Evidence for each mechanistic claim was graded using a four-level evidence scheme (E1-E4), while microbial detection confidence was assessed using a four-tier hierarchy (D1-D4). No component of the proposed axis reached E1 evidence, and all published microbial observations in NSCLC brain metastasis rests on nucleic-acid detection alone. Five mechanisms are examined: circulating microbial metabolites acting on endothelial permeability and glial reactivity; microbiome-imprinted immune-cell trafficking;intracellular bacteria within primary lung tumours; cross-kingdom MR1/MAIT and Dectin-CARD9 signalling; and candidate host genetic determinants. The available human data are small, single-centre and cross-sectional, reporting association with brain-metastasis status rather than prediction or causation; that bacteria accompany disseminating tumour cells into the brain remains a hypothesis awaiting paired sampling, spatial localization and experimental perturbation.We therefore reserve the term prevention for proposed trials, integrate microbial features with established molecular risk models, and specify the genetic-perturbation program and research-only decision pathway that would convert these claims into E1 evidence. The microbiome-brain metastasis axis provides a hypothesis-generating framework for investigating microbial contributions to cerebral dissemination. Multi-centre validation, paired primary-brain metastasis profiling and gnotobiotic models are required before microbiome-directed strategies can be said to improve intracranial outcomes;until then this framework is hypothesis-generating, not practice-changing. The proposed microbiome-brain metastasis axis links gut, lung and intratumoral microbial communities to intracranial dissemination in NSCLC. Current evidence remains insufficient to establish causality, with no proposed mechanism reaching the highest evidence level (E1). Five candidate mechanisms involve microbial metabolites, immune-cell trafficking, intratumoral bacteria, MR1/MAIT and Dectin-CARD9 signalling, and host genetic determinants. Multicentre validation, paired primary and brain metastasis profiling, spatial microbial localisation and experimental perturbation are needed to establish causality and assess clinical relevance. Microbiome-directed prevention and therapeutic strategies remain investigational and should not yet inform routine clinical practice.

items.title: Factors Associated With Early-Stage Pancreatic Cancer: An Analysis of the West Virginia Cancer Registry.
items.abstract: There are limited studies examining factors such as rurality, age, gender, and race, associated with early-stage pancreatic cancer (PC) using population-based data from Appalachia. A cross-sectional study was conducted using patients treated for PC from 1993 to March 2023 and documented in the West Virginia Cancer Registry. Factors associated with early versus late diagnostic stage, including rurality, age, race, gender, and tumor location were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression models. Among 4687 individuals meeting inclusion criteria, 30% were diagnosed with early-stage PC. The majority lived in non-rural counties at time of diagnosis. Most patients did not receive surgery (82%), radiation (89%), chemotherapy (52%), nor immunotherapy (99%) as part of the first course of treatment. Among all cases (n = 7815), 41% received no treatments. Radiation was performed more frequently with early-stage diagnosis (15.6% versus 9.1%, p < 0.0001). Several factors were associated with increased odds of early-stage diagnosis including age (aOR = 1.20; 95% CI 1.05, 1.36) and head of the pancreas as the primary tumor site (aOR = 2.25; 95% CI 1.95, 2.60). Males were at decreased odds of early-stage diagnosis (aOR = 0.85; 95% CI 0.74, 0.98). There were no statistically significant associations between the diagnosis of early-stage disease and rurality (aOR = 0.94; 95% CI 0.76, 1.16). Numerous patients did not receive standard treatment modalities as first course of treatment. Older adults were more likely to be diagnosed with early-stage disease questioning underlying motivators for seeking care. Findings may inform diagnoses of early-stage PC in West Virginia.

items.title: Acute liver failure triggered by hemolytic crisis in a glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficient patient with hepatitis A: A case report.
items.abstract: Hepatitis A virus infection is one of the most common causes of acute viral hepatitis and usually results in a mild, self-limiting illness. (Biju Illolil Kuniyil) However, in rare cases, it can progress to acute liver failure, particularly in vulnerable individuals. Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency is one of the most common enzymatic disorders globally. This X-linked condition predisposes red blood cells to oxidative damage and acute hemolytic episodes triggered by infections, drugs, or foods. (Aradhana Aneja) We report a 53-year-old man who presented with acute hepatitis and subsequently developed severe intravascular hemolysis, acute kidney injury, and acute liver failure. Fractionated bilirubin demonstrated significant indirect hyperbilirubinemia, and lactate dehydrogenase levels were markedly elevated, supporting intravascular hemolysis. A quantitative enzyme assay confirmed glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency. The patient developed coagulopathy and Grade II hepatic encephalopathy, fulfilling diagnostic criteria for acute liver failure. He required intravenous N-acetylcysteine, therapeutic plasma exchange, and hemodialysis. The patient recovered following multidisciplinary intensive care. This case highlights the importance of recognising glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency in patients with viral hepatitis who develop disproportionate anaemia and hyperbilirubinemia.

items.title: Enabling Person-Centred Chronic Hepatitis B Care Among Migrant Men Who Have Sex With Men and Female Sex Workers.
items.abstract: To explore experiences of chronic hepatitis B (CHB) care among migrant MSM and female sex workers attending a specialist sexual health clinic and identify perceived enablers of person-centred care. Qualitative interview study. Semi-structured interviews with 14 overseas-born men who have sex with men (MSM, n = 7) and cisgender and transgender female sex workers (n = 7) attending a publicly funded sexual health clinic in Sydney, Australia. Data were analysed using thematic analysis, with interpretation informed by the Person-Centred Practice Framework. Sexual health services were experienced as safe spaces where CHB was often identified during routine screening, enabling participants to initiate or re-engage with care. Care engagement was shaped by macro-context factors including visa status, Medicare access, language needs, culturally embedded understandings of CHB and referral pathways. Trusting relationships with sexual health practitioners supported discussion of sex, migration and CHB, although some interactions were experienced as directive and overly risk-focused, undermining relational safety. Participants described CHB as having low salience in everyday life but becoming more prominent during intimate moments such as disclosure, partner reassurance and sex work decisions. For some participants, PrEP or HIV therapy offered dual HIV-CHB benefits, making treatment feel more worthwhile and easier to take up. Participants navigated system barriers through peer networks, information-seeking, and services aligned with their needs. Person-centred CHB care for migrant MSM and female sex workers requires more than clinical monitoring. Care should be responsive to the intersecting effects of migration, sexuality, sex work, intimacy and access to health services, while creating culturally and relationally safe environments that support trust, disclosure and sustained engagement. This study calls for embedding CHB care within routine sexual health and HIV care, strengthening language support, improving referral coordination, and supporting clinicians to use reflexive, non-directive communication to avoid moralising or 'risk-only' framings. None.

items.title: Multilevel Determinants of Liver Cancer Screening Uptake in Community-Based High-Risk Populations in Chongqing, China: A Prospective Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Evidence on the uptake and determinants of liver cancer screening in Southwest China remains limited. This study aimed to assess the participation rate, influencing factors, and screening outcomes among high-risk individuals in a population-based liver cancer screening program. A community-based screening program was conducted across 18 districts or counties in Chongqing, China, from October 2013 to October 2022. High-risk individuals identified through a risk assessment system were invited to receive alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) testing and abdominal ultrasonography. A generalized linear mixed model (GLMM) was applied to identify individual-level and structural factors associated with screening uptake. Reasons for non-participation and liver cancer detection rates were also assessed. Among the 369,393 individuals who completed the risk assessment, 37,381 were identified as being at high-risk for liver cancer. After exclusions, 34,647 were included in the final analysis. Of these, 14,062 underwent screening, yielding an uptake rate of 40.59%. Screening participation was significantly associated with younger age, occupational exposures, alcohol consumption, lower levels of physical activity, hepatitis B infection, history of liver cirrhosis, comorbidities, and family history of liver cancer. At the structural level, developed status, use of multiple mobilization strategies, and receiving allowances were positively associated with uptake. Among 20,585 non-participants, the most frequently reported barriers included no symptoms (93.61%), fear of diagnosis (92.60%), and lack of knowledge about cancer prevention and treatment (89.30%). Liver cancer was detected in 14 of the screened individuals, corresponding to a detection rate of 0.10%. Participation in liver cancer screening is shaped by a combination of individual and structural factors. Targeted interventions addressing key barriers (such as low risk perception, fear, and knowledge gaps) and structural factors (such as diversified mobilization and financial incentives) may help improve screening uptake among the high-risk populations. There is limited information about how well liver cancer screening works for people living in Southwest China. We wanted to find out how many high-risk people took part in local liver cancer screening, what factors influenced their decision to participate, and how many liver cancers were found through the program. We studied a community-based screening program covering 18 districts or counties in Chongqing between 2013 and 2022. People at high risk of liver cancer were invited to receive AFP testing and abdominal ultrasound scans. Only around 4 out of 10 high-risk people attended the screening. Participation was higher among younger people, and among those with hepatitis B, liver cirrhosis, a family history of liver cancer, alcohol consumption, occupational exposure to hazards, or multiple comorbidities. People in developed areas, people contacted through multiple mobilization methods, and people who received financial allowances were also more likely to attend. Most people who skipped screening said they had no symptoms, feared being diagnosed, or lacked knowledge about cancer prevention. Among those screened, only 0.10% were diagnosed with liver cancer. Both personal health conditions and structural conditions influence screening attendance. Future efforts should improve risk awareness, reduce fear of diagnosis, and spread health knowledge, while implementing community-level incentives, to increase screening uptake among high-risk residents,which may help find liver cancer at an earlier, more treatable stage.

items.title: Infectious Disease Screening in Hematopoietic Cell Donors: Risk Assessment, Regulation, and Selective Donor Utilization.
items.abstract: Donor-derived infections in hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) are uncommon but potentially severe complications that remain largely preventable through rigorous donor screening and risk mitigation strategies. Although reported incidence appears low, donor-derived infections are associated with substantial morbidity and mortality when transmission occurs in profoundly immunocompromised recipients. In the United States, donor eligibility is governed by Food and Drug Administration requirements for screening and testing for relevant communicable disease agents and diseases. European and international frameworks similarly require comprehensive donor evaluation and testing for major transmissible infections, with additional testing guided by epidemiologic and exposure risk. A key challenge across jurisdictions is distinguishing regulatory donor eligibility from clinical donor suitability and determining when individualized donor-recipient risk assessment is appropriate. Advances in nucleic acid testing have markedly shortened diagnostic window periods for blood-borne pathogens. Concurrently, highly effective antiviral therapies, particularly for hepatitis B and hepatitis C, have transformed select historically prohibitive infections into increasingly manageable risks. These developments have supported selective clinical consideration of donors who remain ineligible under traditional regulatory criteria when an applicable regulatory pathway permits use. This review examines pathogen-specific transmission risk, contemporary screening strategies, and evolving approaches to donor eligibility in HCT. Future donor screening frameworks will likely evolve toward adaptive, pathogen-specific models that integrate molecular diagnostics, recipient mitigation strategies, and real-world transplant outcomes to optimize both safety and donor access.

items.title: Association of GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy with cardiovascular outcomes in patients with MASLD: A translational study.
items.abstract: Patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and type 2 diabetes (T2D) are at increased risk of adverse cardiovascular outcomes, potentially involving systemic metabolic dysfunction and cardiac remodeling. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) improve metabolic dysfunction in MASLD; however, their associations with cardiovascular outcomes and effects on MASLD-associated cardiac remodeling remain incompletely understood. In this translational study, we integrated a real-world TriNetX cohort of patients with MASLD and T2D with complementary experimental studies in a mouse model of MASLD. Following propensity score matching, 42,910 patients were included in each treatment group. GLP-1 RA therapy was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite cardiovascular outcome compared with sulfonylurea therapy (hazard ratio 0.87, 95% confidence interval 0.84-0.91; P < 0.001), although this association was not statistically significant in 90-day and 180-day landmark analyses. In Western diet-fed mice, GLP-1 RA treatment improved selected indices of cardiac function and attenuated cardiomyocyte hypertrophy. Although myocardial fibrosis was numerically reduced, the difference compared with vehicle-treated mice was not statistically significant (P = 0.28). Molecular analyses showed reduced expression of fibrosis- and extracellular matrix remodeling-related markers, including CTGF, TGF-β1, and vimentin. Collectively, GLP-1 RA therapy was associated with lower cardiovascular risk in the primary observational analysis, although this finding was not consistently supported by sensitivity analyses. Complementary experimental findings suggest improvements in selected cardiac functional indices and changes in fibrosis-associated molecular remodeling, warranting further investigation.

items.title: [Construction and internal validation of a prognostic prediction model for R0 resection after conversion therapy in colorectal cancer liver metastases based on clinicopathological features combined with ctDNA].
items.abstract: Objective: To construct and validate an overall survival (OS) prediction model for patients with colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRLM) undergoing R0 resection after conversion therapy. Methods: A total of 364 patients with CRLM who were evaluated by a multidisciplinary team as initially unresectable and underwent R0 resection of both the primary tumor and liver metastases after conversion therapy between January 2018 and December 2023 were retrospectively included with 226 male, 138 female and a median age [ M ( Q 1 , Q 3 )] of 58.0(51.0,66.0) years and randomly divided by computer software at a 7∶3 ratio into a training set ( n =255) and a validation set ( n =109). Follow-up was conducted through February 2026, with OS as the primary endpoint. For model 1, all modelable baseline variables were included in the candidate pool; variable selection was performed using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-Cox regression, and an OS prediction model was constructed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression and presented as a nomogram. Model 2 additionally included the adjuvant chemotherapy regimen variable on the basis of model 1 for sensitivity analysis. Model performance was evaluated using the concordance index (C-index), area under the time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results: The median follow-up was 36.2 months, and 198 deaths (54.4%) occurred. After LASSO selection from the full candidate pool, model 1 included N stage, number of liver metastases, maximum liver metastasis diameter, preoperative carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9) level, KRAS mutation status, BRAF V600E mutation status, postoperative 1-month circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) status, body mass index (BMI), number of conversion therapy cycles, and intraoperative blood loss. Multivariable Cox regression analysis showed that negative postoperative 1-month ctDNA ( HR =0.134, 95% CI : 0.088-0.202, P BRAF V600E wild type ( HR =0.200, 95% CI : 0.106-0.379, P HR =2.564, 95% CI : 1.518-4.332, P HR =1.593, 95% CI : 1.082-2.345, P =0.018) were factors associated with OS after R0 resection following conversion therapy in CRLM. The C-index values of model 1 were 0.759 and 0.773 in the training and validation sets, respectively; the 1-, 3-, and 5-year AUC were 0.808, 0.851, and 0.862 in the training set and 0.850, 0.835, and 0.832 in the validation set, respectively. After stratification by tertiles of the linear predictor in the training set, OS differed significantly among the low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups in both the training and validation sets (log-rank test, all P Conclusion: The combined prediction model established by LASSO selection of all baseline variables has a certain predictive value for OS after R0 resection following conversion therapy in CRLM and can provide a quantitative reference for postoperative risk stratification. 目的： 构建并验证结直肠癌肝转移（CRLM）转化治疗后R0切除患者总生存期（OS）预测模型。 方法： 回顾性纳入2018年1月至2023年12月经多学科团队评估为初始不可切除、接受转化治疗后完成原发灶及肝转移灶R0切除的364例CRLM患者，男226例，女138例，年龄［ M （ Q 1 ， Q 3 ）］为58.0（51.0，66.0）岁，按7∶3比例计算机软件随机分为训练集255例和验证集109例。随访至2026年2月，主要终点为OS。模型1以全部可建模基线变量为候选池，采用最小绝对收缩和选择算子（LASSO）-Cox回归进行变量筛选，采用多因素Cox比例风险回归模型构建OS预测模型并绘制列线图。模型2为模型1基础上再纳入辅助化疗方案变量，进行敏感性分析。通过一致性指数（C指数）、时间依赖受试者工作特征曲线下面积（AUC）、校准曲线和决策曲线分析（DCA）评价模型。 结果： 所有患者中位随访时间36.2个月，共死亡198例（54.4%）。全候选变量LASSO筛选后，模型1纳入N分期、肝转移灶数量分组、最大转移灶直径分组、术前糖类抗原19-9（CA19-9）水平、 KRAS 突变状态、 BRAF V600E 突变、术后1个月循环肿瘤DNA（ctDNA）状态、体质指数（BMI）、转化治疗周期数及术中失血量。多因素Cox回归分析结果显示，术后1个月ctDNA阴性（ HR =0.134，95% CI ：0.088~0.202， P BRAF V600E 野生型（ HR =0.200，95% CI ：0.106~0.379， P HR =2.564，95% CI ：1.518~4.332， P HR =1.593，95% CI ：1.082~2.345， P =0.018）是CRLM转化治疗后R0切除患者OS的影响因素。模型1训练集和验证集C指数分别为0.759和0.773；训练集1、3和5年AUC分别为0.808、0.851和0.862，验证集分别为0.850、0.835和0.832。按训练集线性预测值三分位数分层后，训练集和验证集低危、中危和高危组间OS差异均有统计学意义（log-rank检验，均 P 结论： 基于全基线变量LASSO筛选建立的联合预测模型对CRLM转化治疗后R0切除患者OS具有一定预测价值，可为术后风险分层提供量化参考。.

items.title: Rapid and label-free analysis of biological characteristics of hepatocelluar carcinoma tissues based on histological images.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) exhibits substantial molecular heterogeneity, complicating treatment selection and clinical management. We developed an artificial intelligence-based histopathological framework to predict HCC biological characteristics from routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained slides. Using The Cancer Genome Atlas Liver Hepatocellular Carcinoma (TCGA-LIHC) cohort, transcriptomic phenotypes associated with angiogenesis, stemness, and autophagy were identified through gene set analysis, differential expression analysis, and consensus clustering, and evaluated for overall survival and drug sensitivity. Whole-slide images were processed into 224 × 224-pixel tumor tiles for phenotype prediction using feature extraction (UNI, ResNet50, CTrans, GigaPath, and Virchow2) combined with classic multiple instance learning and clustering-constrained attention-based multiple instance learning.. Models were externally validated at Renmin Hospital of Wuhan University and Tongji Hospital. Interpretability was assessed using attention heatmaps, and predictions were evaluated against molecular markers and tumor differentiation grades. Unsupervised clustering identified two subgroups per phenotype, with significant difference in survival (all p < 0.004) and sensitivities to sorafenib or transcatheter arterial chemoembolization (all p < 0.0001). The tumor detection model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 97.53%. The phenotype prediction models achieved internal optimal AUCs of 85.51%-91.05% and accuracies of 79.63%-88.89%. External optimal AUCs were 70.94%, 88.64%, and 91.17% for angiogenesis, stemness, and autophagy, with accuracies of 62.00%, 78.00%, and 84.00%, respectively. Attention heatmaps revealed distinct morphological features among subgroups, including neovascularization, increased nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, and cytoplasmic vacuolization. Model predictions showed concordance with CD31/CD105 (κ = 0.398-0.432), CD133/LGR5 (κ = 0.428-0.629), Beclin-1/p62-LC3B (κ = 0.592-0.762) (all p < 0.05), and tumor differentiation grade (κ =  - 0.167 to - 0.175, p < 0.05). This proof-of-concept AI framework predicted transcriptome-defined HCC phenotypes from routine histology, with predictions associated with prognosis and therapeutic response. It may provide a cost-effective approach for assessing HCC heterogeneity and complement molecular profiling.

items.title: AURKA, BIRC5 and AURKB as core signature genes associated with endocrine-disrupting chemical exposure in Hepatocellular carcinoma.
items.abstract: This study aimed to systematically explore the molecular mechanisms of Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) induced by endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) and identify core signature genes with clinical utility. Bioinformatics analysis, machine learning, and in vitro experiments were integrated. TCGA-LIHC (The Cancer Genome Atlas-Liver Hepatocellular carcinoma) and GSE76427 datasets were used for target screening and validation. Toxicological analysis, target prediction, functional enrichment, Protein-protein interaction (PPI) network, and three machine learning algorithms were applied to prioritize signature genes. In vitro experiments verified the effects of single EDC on HCC cells and gene dependence. AURKA (Aurora Kinase A), BIRC5 (Baculoviral IAP Repeat Containing 5) and AURKB (Aurora Kinase B) were identified as core signature genes, consistently upregulated in HCC with AUC (area under the curve) > 0.77. Their low expression correlated with better survival rate. EDCs (e.g., MBP) promoted HCC proliferation and invasion, which was dependent on AURKA. Signature genes negatively correlated with anti-tumor immune infiltration. AURKA, BIRC5, and AURKB were identified as candidate biomarkers and therapeutic targets potentially mediating EDC-induced HCC, providing insights into EDC-related hepatocarcinogenesis mechanisms.

items.title: The State of Health in Jordan, 1990-2023: A Systematic Analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study.
items.abstract: Jordan's health system has evolved amid rapid urbanization and the strain of hosting one of the world's largest refugee populations per capita. This study comprehensively evaluates national disease burden trends in Jordan from 1990 to 2023 to inform health priorities. Using the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 framework, we analyzed age-standardized rates of disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), years lived with disability (YLDs), and years of life lost (YLLs) across 370 diseases and 88 risk factors. Data were derived from national censuses, health surveys, disease registries, and hospital records, and harmonized using standardized GBD modeling and estimation procedures. Analyses were stratified by age, sex, and cause. Between 1990 and 2023, age-standardized DALYs declined by 33.88% (95% UI: -37.38 to -30.59), with greater reductions in males (-38.83%; -42.22 to -35.60) than females (-27.22%; -31.33 to -23.58). YLLs decreased by 49.38% (-50.93 to -47.68), while YLDs remained comparatively stable (2.49%; -2.37 to 7.47). Using mutually exclusive GBD Level 3 causes, ischemic heart disease and diabetes mellitus were the two leading causes of DALYs in 2023. Diabetes mellitus rose from 7th place in 1990 to 2nd place in 2023, while neonatal disorders declined from 1st to 7th place. Metabolic risks remained important contributors to the overall disease burden. Jordan's age-standardized diabetes DALY rate in 2023 was approximately 1.56 times the global rate. Jordan's health profile has shifted toward a greater burden from noncommunicable diseases, while age-standardized health loss and premature mortality have declined substantially. In contrast, nonfatal disability changed comparatively little. These findings provide an evidence base for primary prevention of NCDs and for long-term strategies addressing the country's evolving health challenges.
